nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $f_k : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ for $k \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $a \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, we have $|f_k(\omega) - a| < 1/(m+1)$ for all sufficiently large $k$. Then for $\mu$-almost every $\omega$, $f_k(\omega) \to a$ as $k \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Almost sure convergence from shrinking tail bounds

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be pairwise independent measurable sets, let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \to \infty$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\varphi(k)$ be the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the probability of the set of $\omega$ with…
nodes.title: Chebyshev bound along the subsequence

nodes.summary: For a set $s \subseteq \Omega$, the σ-algebra on $\Omega$ generated by the indicator function $1_s : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ (the preimages of Borel sets of $\mathbb{R}$) is contained in the σ-algebra generated by $s$.
nodes.title: The σ-algebra generated by an indicator function

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable sets and let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$. Then $n \mapsto \mathbb{E}[S_n]$ is nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the expected partial sums

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$, let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \to \infty$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\varphi(k)$ be the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}[S_{\varphi(k)}] > 0$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The expected partial sums along the subsequence are positive

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable sets, let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \to \infty$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\varphi(k)$ be the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}[S_{\varphi(k)}] < (k+1)^2 + 1$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the expected partial sums along the subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable sets and let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$. Then $\mathbb{E}[S_{n+1}] - \mathbb{E}[S_n] \le 1$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The expected partial sums grow by at most one per step

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable sets, let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \to \infty$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\varphi(k)$ be the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}[S_{\varphi(k+1)}] / \mathbb{E}[S_{\varphi(k)}] \to 1$ as $k \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Ratios of consecutive subsequence expectations tend to one

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable sets with $\sum_n \mu(A_n) = \infty$, and let $S_n = \sum_{i\lt n} 1_{A_i}$. Then $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Divergent total probability makes the expected partial sums diverge

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be strictly increasing and let $n \ge \varphi(0)$. Then there is $k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\varphi(k) \le n < \varphi(k+1)$.
nodes.title: Bracketing by a strictly increasing sequence

nodes.summary: If two sets $s$ and $t$ are independent with respect to a probability measure $\mu$, then their real-valued indicator functions $1_s$ and $1_t$ are independent random variables with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Independent events have independent indicators

nodes.summary: For every set $s \subseteq \Omega$, the real-valued indicator function $1_s$ satisfies $1_s^2 = 1_s$.
nodes.title: The square of an indicator is itself

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be measurable sets. For every $n$, the partial sum $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$ has expectation $E[S_n] = \sum_{i < n} \mu(A_i)$.
nodes.title: Expectation of a sum of indicators

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a probability measure and $s$ is a measurable set, then the real-valued indicator function $1_s$ lies in $L^2(\mu)$.
nodes.title: Indicators are square-integrable

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure and let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be measurable sets. For every $n$, the partial sum $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$ lies in $L^2(\mu)$.
nodes.title: Partial sums of indicators are square-integrable

nodes.summary: Let $A_1, A_2, \dots$ be pairwise independent events in a probability space with $\sum_n P(A_n) = \infty$, and write $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n 1_{A_i}$. Then almost surely $S_n / E[S_n] \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$, where $E[S_n] = \sum_{i=1}^n P(A_i)$.
nodes.title: Pairwise-independent strong law for indicator sums

nodes.summary: For sets $A_0, A_1, \dots$ in $\Omega$ and every $n$, the partial sum $S_n$, defined pointwise by $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}(\omega)$, equals, as a function on $\Omega$, the sum $\sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$ of the real-valued indicator functions.
nodes.title: The partial sum as a sum of indicator functions

nodes.summary: For sets $A_0, A_1, \dots$ and every $\omega \in \Omega$, the map $n \mapsto S_n(\omega)$, where $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$, is nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Partial sums of indicators are nondecreasing

nodes.summary: For sets $A_0, A_1, \dots$, every $n$ and every $\omega \in \Omega$, the partial sum $S_n(\omega) = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}(\omega)$ satisfies $S_n(\omega) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Partial sums of indicators are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For sets $A_0, A_1, \dots$ in $\Omega$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$ is the sum of the indicators of the first $n$ sets, viewed as a real-valued function on $\Omega$.
nodes.title: Partial sums of indicators

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be subsets of $\Omega$, write $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] = \int S_n \, d\mu \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. If $\varphi(k)$ is the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$, then $\varphi(k) > 0$ for every natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Indices of the quadratic subsequence are positive

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be subsets of $\Omega$, write $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] = \int S_n \, d\mu \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. If $\varphi(k)$ is the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$, then $\mathbb{E}[S_{\varphi(k)}] \ge (k+1)^2$ for every natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the expected count along the quadratic subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be measurable subsets of $\Omega$, write $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] = \int S_n \, d\mu \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. If $\varphi(k)$ is the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$, then $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: The quadratic subsequence is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be subsets of $\Omega$, and write $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$. Assuming $\mathbb{E}[S_n] = \int S_n \, d\mu \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, this is the sequence $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ for which $\varphi(k)$ is the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$.
nodes.title: Quadratic subsequence for the pairwise-independent strong law

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be pairwise independent measurable subsets of $\Omega$, write $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$, and suppose that $\mathbb{E}[S_n] = \int S_n \, d\mu \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $\varphi(k)$ be the least $n$ with $\mathbb{E}[S_n] \ge (k+1)^2$. Then for every real $\varepsilon > 0$, the sum over $k \in \mathbb{N}$ of the probabilities…
nodes.title: Summable deviation probabilities along the quadratic subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $s \subseteq \Omega$ be measurable. Then the indicator function $1_s$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}_\mu(1_s) \le \mu(s)$.
nodes.title: Variance of an indicator is at most its probability

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$ and let $A_0, A_1, \dots$ be pairwise independent measurable subsets of $\Omega$. Then for every $n$, the partial sum $S_n = \sum_{i < n} 1_{A_i}$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(S_n) \le \mathbb{E}[S_n]$, where variance and expectation are taken with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Variance of a sum of pairwise independent indicators is at most its mean

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
